# AgentCard: render the contracted State line + give StateDot an accessible name (D2 ruling)

## Context

Implementing leaf for the **D2 design ruling** on epic neomjs/neo-agent-institution#13 ([ruling](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-institution/issues/13#issuecomment-5012476050)) — the last of the three design-authority items (#15493/D4 and neomjs/neo#15500/D3 shipped). Origin: `#14619`'s audit, re-derived from source before ruling.

## The Problem

Session state reaches the operator by **hue alone**, which WCAG 2.1 **1.4.1 (Use of Color, Level A)** forbids as a sole visual carrier:

- `StateDot.mjs` renders no text, `title`, or `aria-label` — it only swaps a state class.
- `StateDot.scss` gives all seven states **identical geometry** (8px circle); only `--fm-dot` differs.
- `AgentCard.applyRecord` sets **only** the dot (`getReference('state-dot').set({live, state})`) — no state text anywhere in the card or its SCSS.

And the pulse cannot carry the signal: `TOKENS.md:41-43` is correct that the reduced-motion property holds *because* the pulse conveys nothing unique. Re-loading signal there would trade a 1.4.1 failure for a reduced-motion failure.

## The Architectural Reality

The missing channel is **already specified** and simply was never built — `CARD-CONTRACT.md:13`:

> **State line** (mock: "▲ WORKING") | `lifecycle.state` (+ `confidence`) | mono, state-colored; renders the DTO's literal state vocabulary

And the vocabulary resolver already exists: **`stateLabel(state)`**, exported from `HealthSwatch.mjs` alongside the `stateClass` that `StateDot` already imports. `HealthSwatch` proves the pattern in-tree (same class + visible text); `HealthBar` inherits it by composition and is already compliant. The card is the surface that skipped it.

So this is a **conformance gap against a contract we already wrote**, not a new design.

## The Fix

1. Render the contracted **State line** on `AgentCard`, adjacent to the dot, consuming **`stateLabel(state)`** — never a second vocabulary.
2. Give `StateDot` an **accessible name** from the same `stateLabel`. This is 4.1.2 / 1.1.1 — a *separate* criterion. It must not be treated as satisfying 1.4.1: an `aria-label` does nothing for a sighted operator who cannot separate hues. Both are required.
3. Do **not** add shape/glyph-per-state as the primary channel (ruled out: seven distinguishable glyphs in an 8px dot is a legibility problem dressed as an accessibility fix, and it forks the vocabulary). Shape may later reinforce text.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `AgentCard` renders the DTO's literal state vocabulary as text beside the dot; state is legible with colour removed (greyscale check).
- [ ] Text comes from `stateLabel(state)` — no second state→text mapping introduced.
- [ ] `StateDot` exposes an accessible name from the same resolver.
- [ ] `AgentDetail`'s dot (`:192`) covered by the same reasoning or explicitly scoped out with rationale.
- [ ] Card density holds at the measured fleet density — the design judgement this leaf owns (the SSOT mock places a state line; confirm it reads at real row counts).
- [ ] `CARD-CONTRACT.md`'s conformance checklist reflects the now-implemented State line.

## Out of Scope

- The pulse / reduced-motion treatment — deliberately untouched per the ruling.
- D3 / D4 (shipped) · neomjs/neo#15489 (Accounts block) · neomjs/neo-agent-institution#11 (visual-regression harness, the mechanical guard this composes with).

## Related

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-07-18T18:53:10Z

## Narrowed: this leaf is now the 1.4.1 half only — the accessible name split to neomjs/neo#15516

The D2 ruling covers **two different success criteria**, and carrying both here would have meant two PRs against one ticket. The PR-body lint refused that (operator rule neomjs/neo#12367: one `Resolves` per PR mechanically enforces one-PR-per-ticket), and it was right to — the honest resolution is a split, not a `Refs`-only PR.

- **#15516** — the dot's accessible name (**4.1.2 / 1.1.1**) + colocating `stateLabel` into `StateDot.mjs` to avoid an import cycle. Shipped: PR neomjs/neo#15515.
- **this ticket** — the visible **State line** on `AgentCard` (**1.4.1**), reusing `stateLabel` from its new home.

**Why the split is real rather than bookkeeping:** the accessible name is a mechanical contract on a primitive — resolver in, attribute out, unit-testable without a render. The visible channel is a *design* change: it consumes card real estate at measured fleet density, and the SSOT mock's placement has to be confirmed against real row counts rather than assumed. Bundling them would have let the cheap half advertise the expensive one as done.

**The boundary that matters, restated:** shipping neomjs/neo#15516 does **not** close the 1.4.1 finding. An `aria-label` does nothing for a sighted operator who cannot separate the hues. Until this leaf lands, `#14805`'s 1.4.1 gap stays open, and `TOKENS.md:43`'s audit text stays accurate as written.

Revised scope for this ticket: render the contracted State line (`CARD-CONTRACT.md:13`) on `AgentCard` from `stateLabel`, confirm legibility with colour removed, decide the density treatment at real row counts, and update the card contract's conformance checklist. `AgentDetail`'s dot (`:192`) is covered here or explicitly scoped out with rationale.

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-07-18T19:05:55Z

## Implementation spec (design-authority): place the state label beside the dot, not as a separate line

Read `AgentCard`'s vdom to shape this before it's built. The card's own structure makes the placement a real decision, not a mechanical one, so I'm making it here as the D2 authority — so implementation confirms visually rather than decides blind.

### The tension

`CARD-CONTRACT.md:13` specifies a **State line** (*mock "▲ WORKING"*, its own element). But the card is density-governed by construction — its comments are explicit: *"the density contract buys card pixels with exceptions,"* and the lane-row already spends its vertical budget on current-lane + count badge + telltale. Adding a *separate* full-width line for a single state word (`working` / `idle` / `rate-limited` / …) spends a scarce row on low-information-density text.

### The decision

**Render the state label inline, immediately after the `StateDot` in the name-row** — `[dot] [label] [name button] [provenance] [engine]` — rather than as a separate line. Reasons, in priority order:

1. **Strongest 1.4.1 resolution.** The whole failure is that colour is the sole carrier. Placing the text *adjacent to the dot* pairs the two channels at the same glance — the operator reads `● working` as one unit, so the hue is reinforced exactly where it's used. A state line two rows down is a weaker pairing.
2. **Lowest density cost** — one short mono word in an existing row, versus a new row the density contract can't easily afford at 7–17 lanes.
3. **Contract intent satisfied.** `CARD-CONTRACT.md:13`'s intent is *"renders the DTO's literal state vocabulary"* — the adjacent label delivers that; "line" was the mock's layout, not the requirement. Update the field table to record that the state line collapses into the name-row dot-label pair for density, with the conformance checklist gaining a `state-text-present` item.

### Wiring (mechanical, unit-coverable)

- Add a `component` (`fm-card-state`, mono, `flex: none`, `reference: 'card-state'`) right after the `state-dot` in the name-row.
- In `applyRecord`, alongside the existing `getReference('state-dot').set({live, state})`, set `getReference('card-state').text = stateLabel(displayState)` — reusing the resolver now colocated in `StateDot.mjs` (#15516/PR neomjs/neo#15515). No second vocabulary.
- State-colour the text via the existing `fm-state-*` class token, not a literal — it may share the dot's colour binding so text and dot cannot disagree.

### What genuinely needs the render (not fakeable at spec time)

- **Greyscale legibility:** confirm the label reads state with colour removed (the actual 1.4.1 acceptance).
- **Density at real row counts:** confirm the name-row doesn't wrap or truncate the name at 7–17-lane density on a narrow card; if it does, the fallback is a `title`-truncated label or a state *glyph* + text, decided against the render.
- **`AgentDetail`'s dot** (`:192`): same treatment or an explicit scope-out.

This is the half of neomjs/neo#15512 that's design work, not typing — so it stays here with the density judgement, and the wiring above lands with a unit spec (text present, follows state, unknown-state stays literal per the neomjs/neo#15516 resolver contract) plus operator visual validation for the two render-gated ACs.

— Grace (Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Code)

- 2026-07-18T20:15:22Z @tobiu referenced in commit `a854f7a` - "feat(agentos): give StateDot an accessible name and colocate the state-label resolver (#15512) (#15515)

The dot is a graphical indicator carrying session state, but it rendered no text, title or aria-label, so it reached assistive tech as unlabelled decoration. It now exposes role=img plus an aria-label resolved from the shared state vocabulary, set before the cls assignment that flushes the vdom.

stateLabel moves from HealthSwatch.mjs to StateDot.mjs, beside stateToken and stateClass. That keeps the three closed-set resolvers as one source of truth and removes a real hazard: HealthSwatch imports stateClass FROM StateDot, so sourcing the label the other way would have closed an import cycle. HealthSwatch re-exports it, so existing consumers and specs keep their import unchanged.

Scope is deliberately the 4.1.2 / 1.1.1 half only. An accessible name does NOT satisfy 1.4.1 -- it does nothing for a sighted operator who cannot separate the hues. That needs the visible state line CARD-CONTRACT already specifies, which carries a density judgement and stays on the leaf.

New spec pins the name, that it follows a state change so it can never describe a stale state, and that an unknown state degrades to the off TOKEN while its NAME stays literal -- the operator is told what the runtime reported rather than shown a confident benched/offline that did not happen. StateDot + HealthSwatch + AgentCard 28/28.

Refs #15512"

Colour channel, measured not assumed: every --fm-state-* token as TEXT clears 4.5:1 in both skins EXCEPT --fm-state-off (~3.1-3.6:1) — it is dot-tuned to the 3:1 non-text floor, and off/benched is the commonest resting state. So the word renders in --fm-ink-dim (text-safe); the adjacent DOT carries the hue. Decoupling the text colour from the dot tokens means a future dot-retune can't silently push a state word below the text floor.

One vocabulary: stateLabel is the closed-set resolver StateDot names itself with (no card-local string); an unrecognized state passes through as its literal word while the dot degrades to off.
